_source: Third competitive map — the 'urban/tight infantry map' §38 pool slot (design/07-maps.md). Built against the §37 per-map tests and terrain rules in data/terrain.json. Verified by scripts/map-check.mjs (incl. nav-grid reachability).
name: Scrapline
_symmetryNote: Every element has a counterpart at rot(x,y) = (128-x, 128-y); central elements are self-symmetric. Travel-time and resource tests are exact by construction (§37).
tileScale: 1 tile ≈ 4 m; ranges in data/units are in these tiles.
style: tight choke / infantry map (design/07 §38 pool slot). An industrial canyon: one long central scrap-cliff wall splits the map, pierced by two narrow gaps. Forests crowd the gap mouths and a shelf overlooks each gap, so fights are decided by infantry positioning, cover, stealth, and who spots first — not by open-field vehicle sweeps.

resources.note: p1 wood floor — safe, renewable, near-base (§04)
p1 natural-expansion ore — the affordable ceiling, semi-exposed
rich ore in the canyon, west face of the wall between the gaps — mine it under the enemy shelf's gaze
rich ore in the canyon, east face of the wall (rot pair)

highGround.note: scrap-heap shelf over the lower gap; its only ramp faces p1's half, so p2 must fight up it or come around

chokes.note: southern breach in the wall — forest at both mouths, west-shelf overhead; splash/first-strike terrain (§37)
northern breach (rot of lower-gap) — each narrow gap is flanked by the other gap plus its outer rim route
wide route around the wall's southern end — long, exposed, but never contested by the shelves
wide northern rim route (rot of south-rim)

barriers.note: southern span of the scrap wall — ends short of the map edge, leaving the south rim route
central span between the two gaps; the contested rich ores press against its faces
northern span (rot of southern) — leaves the north rim route

forests.note: dense cover at the west mouth of the lower gap — infantry stage here unseen (combat-rules forestConcealment)
cover on the far (east) mouth of the lower gap — ambush ground for whoever pushes through

neutralObjectives.grants: vision + detection over the lower gap
neutralObjectives.note: stands in the breach itself — capturing it strips stealth from the gap fight (§28)

neutralObjectives.grants: vision + detection over the upper gap

airspace: open — aircraft and climb/jump units cross the wall freely; on a map this tight, air and jump infantry are the premium flanking tools (terrain.json highGround.access)

designTests._note: Mirrors terrain.json perMapTestHooks + design/07 §37; asserted by map-check.mjs.
designTests.resourceEquality: each player: 1 wood + 1 natural ore; the canyon rich ore is a symmetric contested pair
designTests.travelTimeEquality: exact by 180° symmetry (§37 tolerance 0 s); both gaps are equidistant from both spawns
designTests.flankAroundEveryNarrowChoke: lower-gap ⇄ upper-gap flank each other, and each also has a wide rim route around the wall's end
designTests.everyPlateauHasARamp: west-shelf and east-shelf each have a ground ramp (on their owner-side approach)
designTests.elevatedArtilleryCannotHitBaseFromSafety: min shelf→base distance ≈ 32 tiles > artillery range 9 ×1.5
designTests.reachability: the wall never touches the map edge and both gaps stay open on the nav grid; BFS proves spawns, resources, and relays are mutually reachable
